cases.title: Calculates the approach distance using one axis

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The approach segment changes in both coordinates, but the calculation considers only one axis.
debugging_steps: Identify whether the route is diagonal.
Use the provided distance helper for a straight segment.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Do both x and y change between the start and the obstacle point?

hint_ladder.hint: One-axis subtraction cannot measure a diagonal.
Call the supplied distance function with the two segment endpoints.

cases.title: Uses half a perimeter and the wrong goal-segment origin
cases.student_code:
perimeter_of_obstacle = width + height
distance_from_obstacle_to_goal = calculate_distance(obstacle_x1, obstacle_y1, goal_x, goal_y)

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The perimeter formula counts only one width and height, and the final path begins from the entry point instead of the specified departure point.
debugging_steps: Write the four sides of a rectangle explicitly.
Confirm the point where boundary following ends.
Calculate the final segment from that point.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: How many widths and heights make a complete rectangle boundary?

hint_ladder.hint: Sketch the rectangle and label all four sides.
Check whether each dimension occurs once or twice in a perimeter.
After the boundary route, use its ending coordinate as the next segment's starting coordinate.

cases.title: Total path double-counts the obstacle approach

expected_feedback.diagnosis: One segment is included twice in the total path.
debugging_steps: Map every addend to that list.
Remove any addend without a distinct traveled segment.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which physical movement does the final repeated term represent?

hint_ladder.hint: Label each addend with the path segment it represents.
Two addends currently describe the same movement.
The approach-distance variable should appear only once in the total.
